title: northvale-retail-edge-deploy-call-capture
body:
Call summary (02/14) with Northvale Retail eng + infra (Tom H, Priya R, ops lead Markus):
- Purpose: quick capture for their Edge/VPC variant evaluation. They want low-latency personalized recommendations at PoS (10ms p95 target per call ideally, realistic target 30ms p95).
- Primary flow: POS device -> northvale edge gateway (k8s on-prem) -> Redwood Private edge connector -> Redwood control plane routing to private inference in their VPC (or dedicated pool depending on scale).

Requirements / asks (explicit):
- VPC peering vs Private Connector: they prefer customer-managed VPC peering (security team) with dedicated subnets for inference nodes. Ask: can Redwood support static IP ranges for peering, and a static set of NAT egress for audit logs?
- PCI scoping: tokenization must occur at POS edge, we must never log PANs. They asked about field-level client-side tokenization SDK; we suggested tokenization before hitting our control plane. Follow up: sample SDK snippet + security whitepaper.
- Model: custom fine-tuned recommender built from their training pipeline. They want to serve a 7B variant quantized to int8 for cost. Concern about QA/regression when quantizing.
- Latency SLOs: regional fallback allowed (if local cluster degraded) but must degrade gracefully to cached suggestions; no user-visible errors.
- Cache semantics: sticky KV cache per-session (session key = device_id + store_id). Important for prefix caching of user history. They want cache TTL of 30m for active sessions.
- Throughput: 1500 requests/min average across 250 stores during peak; concurrency spikes up to 6k concurrent short requests. Need burst handling.

Technical gotchas / red flags noted on call:
- Cold-start penalties on new device sessions (large KV warming cost). Recommend pre-warming for scheduled hours (10am-2pm) using synthetic traffic; need to provide pre-warm runbook.
- POS devices send variable sequence lengths (min 8 tokens, tail up to 512 when history included). Must ensure runtime kernel selection tolerates long tails without dropping to single-threaded path too often.
- Model quantization: their current fine-tuned checkpoints include custom ops (small adapter layers). Need compatibility check; flag: adapter op fused kernel not yet supported in runtime—requires small shim or re-export.
- Networking: some stores have nested NAT and intermittent packet loss. Edge connector must support aggressive retry with idempotency keys. Also, logging level for retries must be tunable to avoid noisy logs in S3.
- Observability ask: per-store cost + latency dashboards, and token-level cost attribution (they will map to internal store P&L).

Notes from security brief:
- They require SSE with customer-managed CMK for all persisted caches and logs. We should confirm Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integration per-store.
- Audit log retention: 7 years for certain events (compliance). Need archival plan (cold storage) and estimated egress costs.

Immediate action items (owner initials + rough ETA):
- AP: assemble short SDK snippet + security whitepaper w/ tokenization recommendation (due 2025-02-18).
- EB: run quick compatibility scan on their model checkpoint (adapter ops) and list re-export options (due 2025-02-19).
- SM: prototype a pre-warm synthetic runner script and estimate cost for 250 stores for 3 months (due 2025-02-21).
- Outreach: schedule deep-technical follow-up with their infra team and our serving-runtime lead (Tom/Kevin) — propose 1-hour deep-dive (target week of 02/24).

Questions to resolve (open):
- Can we guarantee static egress IPs for their VPC peering model? If not, what mitigations (VPN endpoints)?
- Exact format for session identifier (they want to use device_id but some older POS will pad/clone ids). Need robust deduping guidance.
- Quantization regression risk: need to run our Redwood Optimize eval harness on sample prompts — request sample prompt set from Northvale (action: ask them to drop anonymized prompt set into secure bucket).

Loose brainstorming / quick ideas:
- Consider a hybrid approach: local tiny-model fallback on-device for sub-15ms requirements (rule-based or 300M distilled model) + remote full model for best-effort. Would reduce cost and dependency on perfect connectivity.
- Provide a "session warm token" API that allows POS to pre-authorize and warm specific session keys during low-traffic windows. Could integrate with scheduled pre-warm script.
- Autoscale policy suggestion: maintain baseline pool sized for 90% of average, with burst capacity via dedicated hosted pool for spikes (might increase cost but avoid 5-10s tail latencies).

Misc snippets (to paste into follow-up email):
- "We will not ingest PAN data — please ensure tokenization at POS. We can accept tokenized IDs and a hashed device_id for session affinity."
- "To evaluate quantization risk, please upload 200-500 representative prompts/responses from peak hours (anonymized) to secure bucket identified in the linked JIRA."

Meeting tone: pragmatic, a bit protective on security. They are realistic about cost tradeoffs but sensitive to PCI scope. Good rapport overall.

Next steps (external facing plan to send):
1) Provide SDK snippet + security whitepaper (AP)
2) Deliver compatibility report for model (EB)
3) Prototype pre-warm and cost estimate (SM)
4) Schedule deep-technical with runtime lead (Tom/Kevin) and Northvale infra (target 60–90 min)
5) Request anonymized prompt sample and store-level traffic envelope CSV (they will share by 02/19).

Quick informal TODO (my personal):
- Draft the email to Priya with short bulleted answers to PCI + VPC questions (use /templates/pci-answers).
- Add a short line about KMS options and ask legal about 7-year archival liabilities.

End capture.

-- Anika
